There MUST be exactly one item per prepended inherited control wire, followed by one per §9.4 source interface slot, in that order. Each item names a declared class; every bit/cell of a bundle/region has that class. Resolve these classes before capacity and gate matching, and pass actual operand classes into callees. beads.title: §9.4/§11 borrowed owner selection and designated idle sets (borrow_from, gate.ancilla_borrow_from) (from bennett-sched-qm2)
beads.description:
Source: bennett-sched/.tmp/cross-repo-beads.md, "borrowed owner selection and designated idle sets" (local review bead bennett-sched-qm2).

Determination: §9.4 says the caller designates an idle set and §8.2 replaces its owner's charge, but the source call forms and the §11 alloc schema have no owner-selection field and no deterministic default designation, so a checker cannot infer a producer's chosen owner from an opaque frame id. Evidence (C ABI probe): outer mut(t,y), in(x) calls bd(t,x) whose four-CX translation frame borrows b; at capacity 3 it returns INFEASIBLE, at capacity 8/dirty_rate 0.5 it reports time 4, peak 4, occupancy 14; reusing idle caller y would give peak 3 and occupancy 10. Current expansion allocates a separate dirty requirement and records no owner alias. Topology vertices alone do not solve the no-topology case.

Proposed exact schema: extend source alloc decisions with optional borrow_from:[<wire reference>, ...], permitted only for qborrow/dirty acquisitions. A wire reference is exactly one of {invocation:<fully resolved §12.1 context key>,slot:<§9.4 slot id>,bit:<nonnegative integer>} or {allocation:<fully resolved alloc-operation selector>,bit:<nonnegative integer>}. Allocation selectors use the existing fully concrete path/step/phase/generated fields and imply kind=alloc. The array has exactly the acquisition width, in bit order; all referenced bits are distinct, live, held by the direct caller as mutable interface/region bits or live allocation/lease bits, and have the declared/resolved class. Passed callee interface bits, inherited controls, caller read-only slots, overlapping outgoing loans and any owner access overlapping the loan lifetime are forbidden. An incoming lease may be re-lent while held, but its owner must retain the complete lease chain. Unknown references, expired lifetimes, class mismatches or overlapping use reject.

Normative behaviour: supplied borrow_from is the caller's designation. Bind borrowed logical bits to those physical owner bits without acquiring extra physical capacity; retain owner vertices and require alloc.vertices to agree when both occur. Keep every reference-library acquire/release and gate leaf/ordinal unchanged. Require the existing universal T3 condition, including correlated owner states. Split the owner's charging interval around each outgoing loan, replace it by borrower dirty_rate during the loan, count the physical bit once in peaks. A return restores the owner's lease and state. Record aliases by the schedule hash-bound decision, not a producer proof label. For absent borrow_from, specify the existing separate external dirty requirement as the default (no implicit subtraction of an unrelated interface charge), or ratify one deterministic caller idle-set default; current text does not choose. Add class, partial-bundle, nested-lease, read-only/control exclusion, zero-time boundary and topology witnesses, including the exact no-topology t/y/x example.

Analogous gate.ancilla_borrow_from list needed for a selected scheme with dirty ancillae (length equals resolved ancilla count; illegal for native/clean schemes), same exclusions and charging. No unratified field is emitted. This is a contract/mechanics follow-up, not removal of dirty borrowing from scope.

Related: b-isa-spec-wr7, b-isa-spec-4ta, b-isa-spec-7s0.

beads.title: §12.1 adjoint_table lacks a binding to the forward proof/body (from bennett-conformance checker)
beads.description:
Source: bennett-conformance/checker/.tmp/CROSS_REPO_BEADS.md item 5 (sol-checker job; labels requested defect, isa).

Determination: §12.1 adjoint_table lacks a binding to the forward proof/body. §16.3 example 3 says the reverse borrow sequence `cx b t; cx x b; cx b t; cx x b` is not a translation-lemma frame and is covered by adjoint_table, but the structural payload fixes its witness to {} and supplies only integer subclaim indices. §12.3 stores claims per region; variants are opaque producer strings compared bytewise and do not identify a forward body or an adjoint transformation. The text does not say whether a subclaim may name a different region as subject or how a checker binds a forward proof to the reversed region. Guessing that a variant string means adjoint, or accepting an unrelated prior proof, would be unsound; the checker leaves this correspondence unchecked.

Proposed exact replacement in the §12.1 structural payload row: for adjoint_table: { "forward": { "closure_hash", "claim_index" } }. Add immediately after the table: "An adjoint_table witness names a linked forward region and a zero-based claim in that region's certificate record. The checker MUST independently check that claim, then check that the current region's body is the complete §5.3 source adjoint of the named forward body, modulo capture-free renaming of local bindings and positional renaming of interface/classical parameters. Signature widths, region roles, argument types and bounds MUST agree. Primitive adjoints, structured order, unconditional allocations/releases and borrow lifetimes MUST all match; matching only the interface or a chosen basis tuple is insufficient. The forward claim must establish the required preservation/cleanliness relation over the full applicable quantum domain at the same invocation scope; a slice or sampled result cannot discharge a proof obligation. The derived claim inherits that established relation and its proof/evidence scope. Cyclic or unchecked dependencies discharge no obligation. A claim in a region record otherwise names that region as its subject, except the explicitly specified inverse_pair relation. Cross-region structural proof references use the witness above rather than implicit integer indexing."

The spec owner should confirm or replace this binding design; no producer payload extension is accepted before that decision. Related: b-isa-spec-7s0 (borrow-frame claim binding).

beads.title: §3.6 lift.ret delivery scan exceeds the history slot width (EST-SOURCE-03) (from bennett-estimate-bph.6)
beads.description:
Source: bennett-estimate/.tmp/sol-estimate/cross-repo-beads.md, "EST-SOURCE-03: return delivery scans can exceed the history slot" (local bennett-estimate-bph.6).

Determination: ISA 0.9 §3.6 frame layout makes the lift.ret delivery formal N smaller than the actual K25 Globals width at some locations, so the published recipe's R4 delivery loop indexes delivery[4] outside a four-wire actual. Witness tests/fixtures/ret-delivery-source-gap.bisa, object hash b026d3de1b9636bdb7c45deb771f3ccb468fd0e0dbb2bee38da6863500e4d500; pinned ISA document SHA-256 021d5df978f293c36174b73de9facc0884f7502a4bc5c0ab7a621b0ca7071c25. The published VM admits it and returns payload 1/code 0/steps 4 with `run-oracle ... root --input '' --budget 4,1,8,1`. The oracle declares r:reg[1] and an unused ghost:reg[8]; its zero-argument lproc has one reg[1] result; S_cells=3 gives Sc=4, depth_limit=1 gives Dc=2. Call slots have widths (4,4,2), return slots (1,4,2), so §3.6 gives W=(4,4,2) and lift.ret N=4, yet K25 requires the complete Globals list with ghost's width 8. Direct recipe expansion fails at that index; not a VM payload failure.

Proposed exact change (UNADOPTED): append to the §3.6 Frame layout paragraph: "If the instantiated lproc closure contains lift.ret, W_1 is additionally at least W_max (§3.7), including locations that do not occur in a row's write set. The ref lift.ret formal N is this complete W_1-bit disp_1 slot. Every frame retains that width. This makes the complete K25 closure-delivery scan well-typed at every location. Other slot widths remain the maxima of their listed captures and assignments." This widens the witness's first slot 4->8 and its history frame 17->21 bits and changes exact resource costs, so it must be published before a consumer adopts it. An equivalent recipe change bounding each delivery scan by min(width,N) could resolve it instead; no such scalar/formal adapter is specified. The estimator raises EST-SOURCE-03 for positive-B affected requests (CLI pending evidence, no resource rows); B=0 is unaffected.

Related: b-isa-spec-9y4 (same estimator-source-binding family).

beads.title: §3.3/ref qjumpr needs independent address and pc widths (EST-SOURCE-04) (from bennett-estimate-bph.7)
beads.description:
Source: bennett-estimate/.tmp/sol-estimate/cross-repo-beads.md, "EST-SOURCE-04: qjumpr needs independent address and pc widths" (local bennett-estimate-bph.7).

Determination: pinned §3.3 Lifted width rules allow each qjumpr operand any width A with 2^A > n, but the published ref qjumpr has only P and requires both a:wire[P] and succ:wire[P], while §3.6 gives the complete oracle one common pc/successor width. Witness tests/fixtures/jump-width-source-gap.bisa: n=3, two qjumpr rows with address widths 3 and 4, both legal; no single P binds both. Object hash d111d27b9a049d152963dfb76cc2c9365d99b74c4f7eb885894be7ec943ea1ba. Published VM returns payload 1/code 0/steps 3 at input 1,2,1 and tuple 3,0,0,0. Direct recipe binding fails K19 wire-width mismatch; choosing one larger pc width cannot fix two widths and truncation would drop out-of-range high-bit checks.

Proposed exact ref source-binding change (UNADOPTED): qjumpr has separate integer formals P and A: P is the containing oracle's pc/successor width; A is the source address operand's declared width with 2^A > n. Wire formals a:wire[A] and succ:wire[P]. Bind First to the containing instance's first canonical index and End to First plus its row count. Compare a with First and End at width A; bind integer CopyWidth=min(P,A); XOR only those low CopyWidth bits of a into succ, leaving higher succ bits zero when P>A. Preserve the effective fault writes and the §3.6 flagged successor rule. No source wire is resized and no extra state allocation is introduced. Exact JSON-recipe transformation: add A and CopyWidth after P in the integer parameter list; change a.width to A; change every old P occurrence in the current body to A except the bound of the a-to-succ XOR loop, which becomes CopyWidth; keep succ.width=P, First/End and all other parameters. Publish the amended catalog bytes/envelope hash before adoption. The estimator reports EST-SOURCE-04/pending evidence for generated rows needing the missing adapter; B=0 unaffected. The legal source width rule is not to be changed.

beads.title: K81 terminal diagonal inverse versus §6 recompute: owner of the diagonal-phase inverse (from bennett-vm)
beads.description:
Source: bennett-vm/.tmp/sol-vm-queue/cross-repo-beads.md, "ISA 0.9 K81 terminal diagonal inverse versus §6 recompute".

Determination: §6.1 leaves perm provenance unchanged under a diagonal use and §6.4 permits perm-value recompute, while K81 coalesces the maximal terminal matched inverse chain before selecting one cleanup. Counterexample: qalloc d; cx x d; z d; z d; cx x d; qfree d. The written region is identity for both x basis values (and superpositions). Coalescing C=(cx x d; z d), C-adjoint and release, then applying the literal fresh C / XOR / C-adjoint recipe leaves Z on x: for x=1 the original prefix phase survives, whereas written reverse cancels it. The current VM declines recompute for a computing sequence containing Z; that avoids a wrong unitary but is not a ruling on the promised scope, and a blanket ban on these source regions would narrow the contract.

Required normative decision: does the terminal partition exclude diagonal-phase inverse occurrences from the value cleanup, preserving them at their source positions, or does recompute additionally replay/cancel the original phase inverses outside its fresh value computation? Specify exact owner, carrier, caller/callee addresses and phase treatment, including empty/zero-width cases. K81 says every explicit inverse has exactly one owner and no source restriction is added; §6.1 says the value remains perm. Mixed-fat compatibility: this is a local device-module cleanup rule; native host binary/launch boundaries are unaffected (bennett-4ht, fat-object far star: no lock-out). Undisputed K81 cases continue meanwhile.

Determination: dialect 0.2.12 §13.1 specifies no tie-even parity rule for canonical double-double results whose neighbouring lows include zero, so nearest-even is undefined at zero-low transitions. The published high fallback gives L odd high parity; U has odd low significand 1; neither is even. Existing native FMA also reports flags 0 where either nearest result requires 16.

Adjacent canonical pairs (H,0) and (H,2^-1074) have odd/odd parity and equal distance 2^-1075. Both native conversions select the lower pair with flags 24; correct final flags are 16 because the pair total is normal.

Proposed correction: specify zero-low parity, e.g. use the low significand (zero counts as even) whenever either neighbouring low is nonzero, and high significands only when BOTH lows are zero; alternatively a deterministic equal/no-even rule. Preserve the full capability/domain; no arbitrary policy is claimed as conforming. Sqrt cannot reach this half-grid squared midpoint and is independently implemented. Related: b-dialect-spec-dfd (PPCDoubleDouble fallback vs correct rounding), bennett-arith-4yg.

### 4.3 Polyvariant cloning

### 17.1 Memory model

There is one classical memory, shared by H, CC, R and the entry state of every L invocation
(§8.5; NS §3.2):

- **Live allocations**: a shadow-stack frame from its push to its pop (§17.3); a global, always;

### 17.7 The native comparison build

Differential testing (NS §5.1) compares the artefact with the **native comparison binary**: the
materialised device variants, code-generated by the same LLVM major and linked with
`bennett-runtimes` and `bennett-arith` (never host libc or libm) under the comparison link of
§19.5. It is never an `-O0` build: optimisation legally changes marker operands (spike F4), and
the materialised optimised module is the one program both builds implement. The driver MUST make
division by zero and INT_MIN/−1 trap in the native build: on targets whose divide instruction does
not trap it inserts, after materialisation and outside the materialised module, a check that
calls `__bennett_nz_fault` with code 5 or 6. Results compare by the outcome table of §18.7.

**Comparison-only support exception.** Only after the materialised device module has been fixed, the native comparison backend MAY define the three `__bennett_nz_` primitives of §3.1 as native support, and the driver MUST emit `__bennett_rt_native_layout` as specified in §19.5; these definitions MUST NOT enter producer inputs, production device bitcode, region identity or the materialised module used by the ISA map.

The native primitive support MUST reproduce the resolved device addresses, zero fill, live allocation sizes, nonreclaiming allocation/free history and fault outcomes of §§17.1/17.5, with capacity for every history admitted by the resolved heap budget (at most one heap record per byte since max(n,1) ≥ 1), without an arbitrary smaller record cap; host setup/resource failure MUST terminate comparison with an explicit infrastructure failure, never silently relocate the heap, choose defaults, use host malloc, or report a successful dialect outcome.

### 11.4 Host calls from CC

A CC variant's call of an H function (§4.5 item 3) becomes `hostcall bennett.call/<h>` where
`<h>` is the hex SHA-256 of the callee's symbol name: the argument block holds the scalar
arguments (little-endian, in order) and, for each pointer argument whose pointee the analysis
proves pointer-free (no slot holds a pointer atom, §5), the pointee's byte range as an
(offset, length) pair and the bytes themselves. The host-side stub calls the function on a copy,
writes back the bytes of pointer arguments, and replies with the result and the written bytes.
A pointer argument whose pointee may contain pointers read by device code does not become a host
call: the callee is **promoted** to a CC variant (§19.4; ISA-11 would let it stay native, an
efficiency item). Every service is declared in `devices.services` (ISA §9.1, §10).

### 11.5 Fault codes reported from CC

`__bennett_nz_fault(C)` lowers in CC and in R to the ISA instruction `fault C` (ISA §4.1, §4.9, K5): one terminal
record with the exact code (C = 0 reports 4), run `FAILED`, no successor in this activation or any caller, no results, prefix history
retained. No host service is involved. Implicit causes map by ISA §4.9, which agrees with §17.5. On the ISA 0.9 target, an R entry MUST report the exact effective fault cause through the launch result, preserve its entire logical prefix and stop without returning results or running its CC caller's successor. ### 19.2 Mode `--bennett-tier=reversible --bennett-entry=<sym>`

The whole program is the device program in tier R (NS §4.2: "entered through
`__bennett_reversible` or a driver mode"; rungs 3, 5, 6):

- a CC **launch stub** fetches the argv and envp bytes with `hostcall bennett.argv`, initialises
  the shadow stack (§17.3), calls the R entry `<sym>` with (argc, argv, envp), catches the exit
  pseudo-exception (§14.7) and returns the status;
- effects are the ISA device models (§11.2): console, clock, entropy (the launch's entropy tape),
  block with `block_image` from `--bennett-disk=<file>`;
- un-run is `bennett_reverse` (ISA §10): whole-run reversal restores the entry state; tape replay is
  deterministic from the tape and the entropy. Whole-program R mode MUST retain the unmodified entry route and effect tape, and MUST report terminal faults and reverse eligible completed or failed runs according to ISA 0.9. [deps: DLT-19.2, DLT-14.7, DLT-18.6, ISA-4.9-P1, ISA-7.4, ISA-10]
- a `measure` reachable in the program is `BD-E-REVERSIBLE-MEASURE` (§7.5b).

**Process context.** Before entering `<sym>`, the driver/runtimes preparation MUST establish a static single-thread musl process context with the supplied argc/argv/envp bytes, a null-terminated argv and envp, `environ`, program name, initial fenv and the libc/stdio state needed by the linked program; comparison-only Linux `_start` is permitted, but Linux ELF crt/TLS/auxv entry is not required in device tiers.

For a C `main` entry, the runtimes entry wrapper MUST treat normal return as `exit(status)`, running registered exit handlers and flushing stdio exactly once under §14.7 before the launch stub catches the exit pseudo-exception; explicit `exit` follows that same path, and `_Exit` bypasses handlers/flush as §14.7 specifies.

### 19.4 Placement: host vs device CC

their roots (in the limit `main`, and then H is the system-call proxy only: `hostcall
bennett.syscall`). Results are equal by the materialised semantics; ISA-11 would let them stay
native (an efficiency and placement item, §25.3; outline E11).
